scope: All nine Module II LING406 lecture collections reviewed, all 229 sourceText entries, original authoring text, and selected hidden stimulus tables viewed directly. Existing material must remain byte-for-byte unchanged except additive audio UI hooks.
review_mapping: Every item includes reviewPages derived only from data.review section mappings. Renderers can reuse the same section-based audio in individual, combined, core, experiment and review readers, independent of transcript version.
exclusions: l1-critical contains no indispensable source-specified auditory stimulus. Do not add artificial Genie, patient, child, or ASL speech recordings to fill this collection.
Aphasias pp4–6 patient behavior descriptions must not be converted into fake patient audio. New typical-voice readings of comprehension task sentences are acceptable.
Aphasias pp19–22 nonverbal environmental sound examples are visual placeholders without enough exact original stimulus detail. Do not invent source-specific animal/tool sounds.
Development2 pp14–21 joint attention/gaze/intention/mutual exclusivity visual stimulus reconstructions are explicitly deferred by the user. No invented novel labels.
No recordings of ordinary explanatory prose, agenda pages, or reading lists are recommended.
Source example word-by-word sentence pages 18–23 may share full-sentence audio; do not claim the visual ERP protocol was auditory.
New English model readings can make garden-path or ungrammatical examples easier through prosody. Describe them as listening illustrations rather than validated replicas.

items.text: /ba/–/da/–/ga/

items.text: Recent research reported by Ferreira and Clifton in 1986 has demonstrated that syntactic processing is quite independent and that the initial syntactic analysis assigned to a sentence is little influenced by the semantic information already analyzed.
